findings.text: Public acquire records a lock request with subclass and mode flags plus nesting link and caller address. It traces, returns early when disabled, checks the map pointer, takes a limited NMI fallback path when the tracker is disabled, otherwise saves interrupt state and enters recursion protection before calling inner acquire with observed interrupt state and a fresh task sequence.

Public release and sync are thin wrappers around inner logic. Release traces then delegates to inner release and revalidates the chain only on a success signal. Sync behaves like acquire with no try attempt and a marker that requests validation without entering a real critical section, then revalidates the chain.

Held-state and sequence queries expose tracker state without changing it. The held query returns unknown when disabled and otherwise reports held or not held for an optional read versus write distinction. The sequence query returns an all-ones sentinel when disabled or when the map is absent from the current stack.

Pin family lets callers protect a held entry against release checking. Pin creates a nonzero cookie from scheduler time and adds it to the matching entry. Repin adds a prior cookie value again. Unpin subtracts and clamps on corruption. All wrappers preserve interrupts and use recursion protection and no-op with a nil cookie when disabled.

Class reassignment and downgrade mutate a held entry then replay later entries. Both wrappers save interrupts, guard recursion, validate flags, invoke the inner routine and revalidate the chain on success. Reassignment reinitializes map identity and class; downgrade marks the entry as read and updates caller address.

Diagnostics include a system-wide held-lock dump, a tracker reset, and a read-recursion predicate. The dump skips output when disabled and otherwise walks every thread under read-side protection while petting watchdogs. Reset clears current task state and chain counters and tables and re-enables checking. The predicate reports true under a force flag, without queued reader-writer support, or in interrupt context.

Inner held test scans the current task stack from oldest to newest and compares each slot against a target map. On a match it distinguishes an exact read-mode match from a mode mismatch when the caller requests a specific mode, and reports a wildcard match when the caller passes negative one. Absence reports not held.

Class operation accounting has two build variants at the same logical name: one derives an index from the class address relative to the class table and increments a per-class counter, and one expands to no operation. Callers invoke it unconditionally after class resolution.

Class identity is resolved per subclass with a small cache. Low subclass values first consult a per-map cache slot and validate it; on miss or high subclass the tracker registers or looks up a class and aborts the acquisition quietly when registration fails. Invalid subclass range also aborts.

Two distinguished keys alter tracking. A no-track key bypasses acquisition and release entirely. A no-validate key, or globally disabled proof mode, forces the check flag off for that acquisition and counts a no-check event while still recording the entry.

Dependency identity is an incremental chain value carried per task. Empty stacks must carry the initial value and start a new head. Each acquisition saves the prior value in the new slot, optionally restarts the chain on interrupt-context separation, then mixes the new holder identity into the running value. Successful commit stores the new value; middle-stack removal and mutation truncate depth and restore the saved prior value before replay.

Repeated acquisition of the same class at the top of a nonempty stack can merge instead of pushing when a nesting lock is supplied. The logic bumps reference counts on both the incoming request and the existing top entry, guards against counter wrap, and returns a distinct merged outcome without changing depth.

Synchronization-only acquisition runs class, context, usage and chain validation but never commits depth. It returns success after validation so callers can express ordering against locks that are not actually held in the current critical section.

Mutation and non-innermost release rebuild the tail by replaying saved slots through inner acquire. Replay preserves original mode, check, interrupt, nesting, caller, reference, pin and sequence attributes. A validation failure during replay aborts with an error signal; a merge during replay is counted only when it affects the first replayed slot.

Pin accounting is additive per held slot. Cookies are small nonzero random values that permit nesting in a wider counter. Unpinning requires a positive counter and a matching held entry; negative results warn and clamp to zero. Sequence values are assigned from a per-task monotonic counter at acquire time and stored per slot.

When the tracker is disabled in NMI context without recursion, a non-try acquisition still performs a limited unused-state check with a transient holder description rather than recording. Ordinary contexts return immediately when disabled.

Unused-state verification only applies under proof mode and when the map already has a class. Write acquisitions conflict with both plain use and read use, while read acquisitions conflict only with plain use, allowing read-only reuse patterns. A conflict rewrites the transient slot class index and reports a usage violation.

Class removal scans every chain hash bucket and drops each chain containing the target class at most once. Removal frees per-chain holder storage, overwrites the chain key for concurrent readers, decrements the per-context chain count, unlinks with RCU semantics, marks the chain index in a pending-free bitmap, and bumps a zapped-chain counter.

All public wrappers share one discipline: early disabled check, save interrupt state, validate flags, enter recursion guard, call inner logic, leave recursion guard, restore interrupts. Inner acquire additionally records whether interrupts were off at entry. This keeps tracker state consistent against reentry and interrupt arrival.

Tail replay requires interrupts disabled and warns otherwise. System-wide dump holds RCU read protection while iterating all threads. Chain removal iterates buckets under RCU read protection and unlinks with RCU-safe deletion, making traversal safe against concurrent readers.

Each held slot stores class index, caller address, map pointer, nesting pointer, interrupt context, try and read and check and sync and interrupt-off modes, reference count, pin count, sequence number, prior chain value, and optional timing stamps. The per-task tracker stores the slot array, current depth, running chain value and sequence counter.

Auxiliary state includes a pin cookie holding an opaque value with a distinguished nil value, a dependency chain with base offset and depth plus chain key and interrupt context and hash linkage, and global tables for classes, chains, chain hash buckets and per-context chain counts.

Inner acquire returns three outcomes: failure, committed or validated success, and merged. Failure leaves depth unchanged. Success either commits depth and chain value or, for sync markers, validates without committing. Merged leaves depth unchanged while accumulating references. Replay maps inner failure to a replay-error signal and otherwise completes with success.

Inner release first rejects empty stacks and unknown maps as imbalance errors. It records hold time on exact instance match, warns when releasing pinned entries, and consumes one reference when references remain; if references still remain the stack is unchanged. Otherwise it truncates to the removed slot, restores its prior chain value, fast-paths innermost removal, and replays later slots.

Global checking has enabled, silent-disabled and off states. Many paths return immediately when off. Depth overflow, imbalance reporting and some violations turn checking off, with verbose paths dumping held state and stacks. Reset clears current task and hash state and turns checking back on with zeroed context counts.

Overflow past the maximum depth disables checking and emits diagnostics including task depth, held locks, all locks and a stack trace. The tracker also tracks a high-water depth. Callers must size the maximum depth for the deepest legitimate nesting.

Misuse warnings cover unlocking with an empty stack or unknown lock, supplying a nesting lock that is not currently held, downgrading an already-read lock, releasing a pinned lock, and pinning or unpinning unheld or unpinned entries including corrupted negative pin counts. Imbalance reporting is suppressed when already off or in silent mode.

The fragments use symbolic limits and sentinels whose numeric values are not shown here: maximum stack depth, maximum subclasses, number of cached classes, initial chain key, held versus not-held versus unknown states, read-mode wildcard, all-ones unknown sequence, usage and read-use flags, and per-context chain counters. Implementations must treat them as named constants.
